Q1: Where should the "labelled `ai:clarification` but no clarify output" detection live, and which threshold should it use?
Choices:
A) Extend the existing standalone stall-recovery loop. When an `ai:clarification` issue has no clarify output, re-run clarify once (posting a `/reclarify` comment with a marker) instead of `auto_respond_clarify`. On the second miss, use the existing `escalate_human`. Keep the existing threshold (`STALL_THRESHOLD_CLARIFICATION_MINUTES`, default 60 min). (RECOMMENDED)
B) Same branch inside the existing loop, but with a new threshold variable that defaults to 6 hours. Until that threshold passes, the existing 60-minute auto-answer is turned off for issues with no clarify output.
C) Add a separate new scan exactly as the issue describes (6-hour default) and leave the existing loop unchanged. Both paths could then act on the same issue.
Q2: How should the new detection treat `ai:clarification` issues that the security-dependency gate (`security_dependency.py` verdict `held`) is holding back on purpose? Right now these stay silent with no comment, which may be exactly what happened to #146.
Choices:
A) Keep the hold and don't re-run clarify. Post one advisory comment with a marker naming the blocking dependency issue, so a held issue doesn't look stalled. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Keep the hold silently: the new detection skips held issues entirely, the same as today.
C) Re-run clarify even when the gate reports `held`. Note: this bypasses the same-file security ordering gate.
